title: Advanced Aquaculture
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 400L Advanced Aquaculture curriculum: advanced/high-technology culture systems (recirculating aquaculture systems, biofloc, cage culture at scale), broodstock genetics and selective breeding, advanced feed formulation and nutrition, advanced water quality/system management, and emerging culture species. Builds on and goes beyond Aquaculture Systems & Pond Management (FIS307), which covers basic pond-based systems; kept distinct from Integrated Fish Farming (FIS407) by focusing on standalone high-tech aquaculture rather than fish-livestock/crop integration.

questions.question: A Recirculating Aquaculture System (RAS) is defined by its use of:
options: Mechanical and biological filtration to treat and reuse a large proportion of culture water
Complete daily replacement of all pond water from a river
Open ocean cages with no water treatment
Only sunlight as the sole means of water purification
questions.correct_answer: Mechanical and biological filtration to treat and reuse a large proportion of culture water
questions.explanation: RAS technology treats and recirculates most of the system's water through mechanical and biological filters, greatly reducing water use compared to flow-through or pond systems.

questions.question: The biofilter in a RAS is essential mainly because it:
options: Houses nitrifying bacteria that convert toxic ammonia into less harmful nitrate
Filters out only large solid debris
Adds oxygen directly through chemical reaction
Cools the water temperature to freezing
questions.correct_answer: Houses nitrifying bacteria that convert toxic ammonia into less harmful nitrate
questions.explanation: The biofilter provides surface area for nitrifying bacteria to convert toxic ammonia to nitrite and then to the much less toxic nitrate, a process called nitrification, critical for maintaining water quality in recirculated systems.

questions.question: Nitrification in a biofilter occurs in two main bacterial steps:
options: Ammonia to nitrite (by Nitrosomonas-type bacteria), then nitrite to nitrate (by Nitrobacter-type bacteria)
Nitrate directly to ammonia in a single step
Oxygen to carbon dioxide
Nitrogen gas directly to ammonia with no bacteria involved
questions.correct_answer: Ammonia to nitrite (by Nitrosomonas-type bacteria), then nitrite to nitrate (by Nitrobacter-type bacteria)
questions.explanation: Nitrification is a two-step microbial process: ammonia-oxidizing bacteria convert ammonia to nitrite, and nitrite-oxidizing bacteria then convert nitrite to the less toxic nitrate.

questions.question: Biofloc technology in aquaculture relies on maintaining a high carbon-to-nitrogen (C:N) ratio in the water mainly to:
options: Stimulate heterotrophic bacteria to assimilate ammonia into microbial protein (floc) that fish can consume
Increase water salinity to marine levels
Eliminate the need for any aeration
Reduce the water temperature significantly
questions.correct_answer: Stimulate heterotrophic bacteria to assimilate ammonia into microbial protein (floc) that fish can consume
questions.explanation: Biofloc systems add a carbon source to raise the C:N ratio, encouraging heterotrophic bacteria to rapidly assimilate ammonia into bacterial biomass (floc), which simultaneously controls water quality and supplies supplementary protein feed.

questions.question: A key advantage of biofloc technology over conventional pond culture is:
options: Reduced water exchange requirements and in-situ conversion of waste nutrients into feed protein
Complete elimination of the need for any stocking of fish
Guaranteed zero mortality of cultured stock
No requirement for aeration at any stocking density
questions.correct_answer: Reduced water exchange requirements and in-situ conversion of waste nutrients into feed protein
questions.explanation: By converting nitrogenous waste into bacterial floc that serves as supplementary feed, biofloc systems can operate with minimal water exchange while also reducing overall feed costs, though they require intensive aeration.

questions.question: Large-scale cage culture in reservoirs or lakes, compared to small-scale cage culture, requires particular attention to:
options: Carrying capacity of the water body to avoid cumulative nutrient loading and self-pollution
Complete elimination of any feeding regime
Avoiding any use of nets or cage structures
Ensuring zero water flow through the cages
questions.correct_answer: Carrying capacity of the water body to avoid cumulative nutrient loading and self-pollution
questions.explanation: As cage culture is scaled up within a water body, the cumulative nutrient loading from feed and waste can exceed the water body's assimilative capacity, causing self-pollution and degraded conditions for the caged fish themselves.

questions.question: Selective breeding programs in aquaculture aim to improve target traits such as growth rate primarily by:
options: Choosing broodstock with desirable genetic traits to be parents of the next generation
Randomly selecting broodstock with no reference to performance
Eliminating the need for record-keeping on parentage or performance
Crossing only genetically identical individuals in every generation
questions.correct_answer: Choosing broodstock with desirable genetic traits to be parents of the next generation
questions.explanation: Selective breeding involves systematically choosing individuals with superior heritable traits (e.g., faster growth, disease resistance) as broodstock to gradually improve those traits in subsequent generations.

questions.question: Heritability, a key concept in selective breeding, refers to:
options: The proportion of variation in a trait among individuals that is due to genetic differences
The total number of offspring a fish can produce
The exact age at which a fish reaches sexual maturity
The color pattern of a particular fish species
questions.correct_answer: The proportion of variation in a trait among individuals that is due to genetic differences
questions.explanation: Heritability estimates what fraction of the observed variation in a trait (such as growth rate) is attributable to genetics rather than environment, guiding how effectively selection can improve that trait.

questions.question: Inbreeding depression, a risk in poorly managed hatchery broodstock programs, refers to:
options: Reduced fitness (e.g., growth, survival, fertility) resulting from mating between closely related individuals
An improvement in growth performance from mating relatives
A disease unrelated to genetics
A deliberate breeding technique used to boost genetic diversity
questions.correct_answer: Reduced fitness (e.g., growth, survival, fertility) resulting from mating between closely related individuals
questions.explanation: Repeated mating among closely related fish increases homozygosity of deleterious recessive alleles, often reducing growth, survival, and reproductive performance, known as inbreeding depression.

questions.question: Genetically Improved Farmed Tilapia (GIFT) is a well-known example of:
options: A selectively bred tilapia strain developed for superior growth performance
A genetically modified organism created through gene-splicing techniques
A wild, unimproved tilapia population
A disease-resistant catfish strain
questions.correct_answer: A selectively bred tilapia strain developed for superior growth performance
questions.explanation: GIFT tilapia was developed through a classical selective breeding program (not genetic engineering) that combined and selected among tilapia strains over generations to significantly improve growth rate.

questions.question: Monosex (all-male) tilapia populations are often preferred in advanced aquaculture production mainly because:
options: They avoid uncontrolled breeding in grow-out ponds, which stunts growth due to overcrowding
Female tilapia grow significantly faster than males in all cases
Monosex populations require no feed input at all
Mixed-sex populations always produce higher total yield
questions.correct_answer: They avoid uncontrolled breeding in grow-out ponds, which stunts growth due to overcrowding
questions.explanation: Male tilapia generally grow faster than females, and if both sexes are stocked together they breed prolifically, leading to overcrowding and stunted growth; all-male populations avoid this by preventing reproduction during grow-out.

questions.question: Hormonal sex reversal in tilapia culture, commonly using methyltestosterone-treated feed, is applied to fry mainly to:
options: Produce predominantly male populations for faster, more uniform grow-out
Permanently sterilize all fish in the population
Eliminate the need for any further feeding
Change the fish species entirely
questions.correct_answer: Produce predominantly male populations for faster, more uniform grow-out
questions.explanation: Feeding sex-reversal hormone to tilapia fry during the labile period of sexual differentiation converts genetic females into phenotypic males, producing all-male populations for improved growth uniformity.

questions.question: Advanced fish feed formulation aims to balance which key nutrient categories for optimal growth?
options: Protein, lipids, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals in appropriate proportions
Only protein, with all other nutrients ignored
Water content exclusively
Coloring agents only
questions.correct_answer: Protein, lipids, carbohydrates, vitamins, and minerals in appropriate proportions
questions.explanation: A well-formulated aquafeed must supply balanced levels of protein, lipid, carbohydrate energy, vitamins, and minerals matched to the species' and life stage's specific nutritional requirements.

questions.question: Essential amino acids in fish nutrition are those that:
options: Cannot be synthesized by the fish in sufficient quantity and must be supplied in the diet
Are entirely unnecessary for fish growth
Can always be synthesized by the fish regardless of diet
Are only relevant to marine, not freshwater, fish species
questions.correct_answer: Cannot be synthesized by the fish in sufficient quantity and must be supplied in the diet
questions.explanation: Essential amino acids must be obtained from the diet because the fish cannot synthesize them (or enough of them) internally, making their inclusion in formulated feed critical for growth and health.

questions.question: Least-cost feed formulation software is used by advanced aquafeed manufacturers primarily to:
options: Determine the combination of ingredients meeting nutritional requirements at the lowest possible cost
Randomly select ingredients regardless of nutrient content
Eliminate the need for any nutritional analysis of raw materials
Set only the price of the finished feed, ignoring nutrient content
questions.correct_answer: Determine the combination of ingredients meeting nutritional requirements at the lowest possible cost
questions.explanation: Least-cost formulation uses mathematical optimization (e.g., linear programming) to identify the ingredient mix that satisfies all nutrient specifications for a target species at minimum cost.

questions.question: Fishmeal replacement research in aquafeed formulation, using ingredients such as soybean meal or insect meal, is driven mainly by the need to:
options: Reduce reliance on and cost of wild-caught fishmeal while maintaining nutritional adequacy
Increase the fishmeal content of feed to 100 percent
Eliminate protein entirely from fish diets
Guarantee that fish will refuse to eat the feed
questions.correct_answer: Reduce reliance on and cost of wild-caught fishmeal while maintaining nutritional adequacy
questions.explanation: Because fishmeal is costly and derived from wild fish stocks, research focuses on identifying alternative protein sources that can partially or fully replace fishmeal while still meeting the cultured species' nutritional needs.

questions.question: Extrusion processing of aquafeed pellets, compared to simple pelleting, offers the advantage of:
options: Producing floating or slow-sinking pellets with improved digestibility and water stability
Making all pellets sink immediately and dissolve within seconds
Removing all nutritional value from the ingredients
Eliminating the need for any ingredient mixing
questions.correct_answer: Producing floating or slow-sinking pellets with improved digestibility and water stability
questions.explanation: Extrusion cooking gelatinizes starches and can create buoyant pellets, improving feed digestibility, water stability, and allowing farmers to observe feeding activity, an advantage over simpler pelleting methods.

questions.question: In advanced RAS management, a drop in biofilter efficiency (e.g., after a chemical treatment) most immediately risks:
options: A spike in toxic ammonia or nitrite concentrations harming the cultured fish
An immediate increase in fish growth rate
Complete elimination of any need for future monitoring
Automatic improvement in water clarity
questions.correct_answer: A spike in toxic ammonia or nitrite concentrations harming the cultured fish
questions.explanation: If the nitrifying bacterial population in the biofilter is disrupted (e.g., by antibiotics or chlorine), ammonia and nitrite can rapidly accumulate to toxic levels since the system relies on continuous biological treatment.

questions.question: Oxygen supersaturation systems (such as pure oxygen injection) are used in advanced intensive aquaculture mainly to:
options: Support much higher stocking densities than aeration with atmospheric air alone can sustain
Completely replace the need for any water treatment
Lower the water temperature significantly
Eliminate the need for feeding fish
questions.correct_answer: Support much higher stocking densities than aeration with atmospheric air alone can sustain
questions.explanation: Pure oxygen injection can achieve dissolved oxygen levels beyond what is possible with standard air-based aeration, enabling the very high stocking densities used in intensive RAS and other advanced systems.

questions.question: Off-flavor (earthy/musty taint) sometimes found in intensively or pond-raised fish is commonly caused by:
options: Compounds such as geosmin and 2-methylisoborneol produced by certain algae and bacteria
Excess dissolved oxygen in the water
The use of high-quality commercial feed
A deficiency of dietary vitamin C
questions.correct_answer: Compounds such as geosmin and 2-methylisoborneol produced by certain algae and bacteria
questions.explanation: Geosmin and 2-methylisoborneol (MIB), produced by cyanobacteria and actinomycetes, are absorbed by fish and can impart an earthy or musty off-flavor, a recognized quality issue managed through depuration or system control.

questions.question: Depuration, sometimes used before marketing intensively raised fish with off-flavor concerns, involves:
options: Holding fish in clean, off-flavor-free water for a period to allow taint compounds to clear from the flesh
Adding artificial flavoring to mask any off-taste
Freezing fish immediately without any holding period
Increasing feeding rate immediately before harvest
questions.correct_answer: Holding fish in clean, off-flavor-free water for a period to allow taint compounds to clear from the flesh
questions.explanation: Depuration involves transferring fish to clean water for a period before harvest, allowing accumulated off-flavor compounds like geosmin to be metabolized or excreted, improving final product quality.

questions.question: Broodstock nutrition, particularly the inclusion of essential fatty acids, is important in advanced aquaculture hatcheries mainly because it:
options: Directly affects egg quality, fertilization rate, and larval survival
Has no impact on any aspect of reproduction
Only affects the broodstock's own body color
Prevents the need for any hormone-induced spawning technique
questions.correct_answer: Directly affects egg quality, fertilization rate, and larval survival
questions.explanation: Broodstock diet, especially essential fatty acid and vitamin content, strongly influences egg quality, fertilization success, and subsequent larval viability, making broodstock nutrition a key focus in advanced hatchery management.

questions.question: Integrated Multi-Trophic Aquaculture (IMTA), an emerging advanced aquaculture concept, involves:
options: Co-culturing species from different trophic levels so that waste from one becomes a resource for another
Culturing only a single species at extremely high density
Eliminating all interaction between cultured organisms
Farming exclusively terrestrial livestock alongside fish with no aquatic link
questions.correct_answer: Co-culturing species from different trophic levels so that waste from one becomes a resource for another
questions.explanation: IMTA combines fed species (e.g., fish) with extractive species (e.g., filter-feeding shellfish or seaweed) that use the fed species' waste nutrients, improving overall resource use efficiency and reducing environmental impact.

questions.question: Emerging/alternative species culture research in aquaculture, such as exploring new indigenous species for farming, is driven partly by the goal of:
options: Diversifying production and reducing overreliance on a narrow range of currently farmed species
Eliminating all currently farmed species from production
Avoiding any further research into fish biology
Increasing dependence on a single globally dominant species
questions.correct_answer: Diversifying production and reducing overreliance on a narrow range of currently farmed species
questions.explanation: Exploring the culture potential of additional indigenous or underutilized species helps diversify aquaculture production, spread risk, and potentially open new markets, rather than relying solely on a few dominant species like tilapia and catfish.

questions.question: Real-time water quality monitoring sensors (for dissolved oxygen, pH, temperature) in advanced aquaculture systems provide the main benefit of:
options: Enabling rapid detection of and response to deteriorating conditions before they harm the stock
Completely replacing the need for a farm manager
Eliminating the biological requirement for oxygen in cultured fish
Guaranteeing zero equipment failure at all times
questions.correct_answer: Enabling rapid detection of and response to deteriorating conditions before they harm the stock
questions.explanation: Continuous automated monitoring allows farm managers to detect water quality problems (e.g., a drop in dissolved oxygen) quickly and respond (e.g., activate backup aeration) before stock is harmed, especially critical in high-density systems with little buffering capacity.

questions.question: A major operational risk specific to high-density RAS and biofloc systems, compared to extensive pond systems, is that they:
options: Have little buffering capacity, so equipment failure (e.g., aeration or pump loss) can cause rapid, catastrophic stock loss
Never require any electricity or mechanical equipment
Are inherently immune to any disease outbreak
Require no monitoring once established
questions.correct_answer: Have little buffering capacity, so equipment failure (e.g., aeration or pump loss) can cause rapid, catastrophic stock loss
questions.explanation: Because high-density intensive systems operate with much less water volume relative to biomass than extensive ponds, they have limited buffering capacity; a power or equipment failure can lead to rapid oxygen depletion and severe losses.

questions.question: Sperm cryopreservation in advanced fish hatchery genetics programs is valuable mainly because it allows:
options: Long-term storage of genetic material for use in breeding programs even when males are unavailable
Immediate reversal of any water quality problem
Complete elimination of the need for female broodstock
Guaranteed disease-free offspring in every case
questions.correct_answer: Long-term storage of genetic material for use in breeding programs even when males are unavailable
questions.explanation: Cryopreserving milt (sperm) allows genetic material from valuable males to be stored and used later, supporting genetic conservation, selective breeding logistics, and flexibility when synchronizing broodstock availability.

questions.question: Solids removal (mechanical filtration) is typically the first treatment stage in a RAS water loop mainly because uneaten solid waste:
options: Rapidly decomposes and degrades water quality if left in suspension, and can clog downstream biofilters
Has no effect on water quality if left untreated
Improves dissolved oxygen levels on its own
Only needs to be removed once per year
questions.correct_answer: Rapidly decomposes and degrades water quality if left in suspension, and can clog downstream biofilters
questions.explanation: Solid wastes such as feces and uneaten feed decompose quickly, consuming oxygen and releasing ammonia, and can physically clog or foul biofilter media, so mechanical solids removal is typically placed early in the treatment train.

questions.question: A protein skimmer (foam fractionator), sometimes used in marine RAS, removes dissolved organic compounds mainly by:
options: Using fine air bubbles that bind organic molecules and carry them to a collection cup as foam
Freezing the water to precipitate organic matter
Adding chlorine to destroy all organic compounds
Heating the water to boiling point
questions.correct_answer: Using fine air bubbles that bind organic molecules and carry them to a collection cup as foam
questions.explanation: Protein skimmers inject fine bubbles into the water column; dissolved organic molecules adhere to the bubble surfaces and are carried upward as foam into a collection cup, removing them before they break down into ammonia.
